claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure.
The reported heterostructure includes distinct phase distributions.
The reported heterostructure includes relevant grain-boundary characteristics or networks.
The proposed PIML model will use descriptors derived from high-resolution microstructural imaging and compositional mapping.
The proposed PIML model will incorporate continuum-mechanics constraints.
Quantified phase distributions and grain-boundary networks influence the mechanical response of HfNbTiVAl10.
Coupling physical models with microstructural feature extraction enables the PIML model to approximate stress-strain response.
The proposed model can predict crack-initiation behavior.
The proposed model can predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture-related responses.
The PIML model will be more accurate than continuum finite-element simulations lacking enhanced microstructural inputs.
The PIML model will reduce predictive errors by at least 10–20% relative to the finite-element baseline.
The PIML model will be orders of magnitude faster than the finite-element baseline.
PIML predictions will take seconds whereas established finite-element simulations will take hours.
Predictive performance may deteriorate for heterogeneities, strain rates, or temperatures outside the training-data regime.
The effectiveness of the model may depend on the precision of the microstructural descriptors.
Predictions from the PIML and finite-element models will be compared against tensile and fracture measurements on the same independently tested samples.
Failure to achieve at least a 10% accuracy improvement and a substantial time reduction from hours to seconds across multiple independent samples will falsify the hypothesis.
